[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of existing literature on remote collaboration and ideation (e.g., studies on brainstorming, online suggestion systems, and virtual teams) focusing on productivity metrics and evaluation biases. — Synthesizes prior findings across contexts to assess whether systematic undercounting of asynchronous text-based contributions is supported or refuted, providing broader evidence for the claim.

[PATH:empirical] Observational study using archival performance review data from global tech firms, comparing evaluation scores of employees who primarily contribute asynchronously vs. synchronously, controlling for role and tenure. — Tests the hypothesis in real-world organizational settings post-2020, directly assessing whether standardized metrics systematically undervalue asynchronous contributors in performance reviews.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of existing studies on remote collaboration and innovation measurement, focusing on the correlation between metric design (e.g., reliance on text-based artifacts vs. video recordings) and the perceived or measured contribution of different communication modes. — Synthesizes prior evidence to assess whether the hypothesized bias is consistently observed across different contexts, and identifies moderating factors such as team size, task complexity, and evaluation criteria.
